item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
The line m is a line of symmetry for figure ABCDE.

The measure of angle BCD is

[Image: Polygon ABCDE with line of symmetry m]
item.figure_description: A symmetric five-sided polygon ABCDE with a vertical dashed line of symmetry labeled m, which has arrows at both top and bottom ends. The horizontal top side connects vertex A on the left to vertex E on the right, bisected perpendicularly by line m. The left side goes down and outward from A to vertex B, then slants down and inward to vertex C at the bottom, which lies on line m. The right side is a mirror image, going from E down and outward to vertex D, then down and inward to vertex C. Inside the polygon, angle A is marked with an arc and labeled 130, angle B is marked with an arc and labeled 110, and the angle between side BC and line of symmetry m at vertex C is marked with an arc and labeled 30.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Geometric figure with parallel lines and triangle]

In this figure, line l is parallel to line m. The measure of angle DAC is 55°.
What is the value of x + y?
reference_items.figure_description: Two horizontal parallel lines are shown: line l on top and line m on the bottom. Points A and D lie on line l, with D to the right of A. Points B and C lie on line m, with C to the right of B. Line segments AB and AC connect the two lines, forming triangle ABC. A dashed arc indicates that angle DAC measures 55°. Inside triangle ABC, angle BAC at vertex A is marked with an arc labeled x°, and angle ABC at vertex B is marked with a dashed arc labeled y°.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Geometric diagram]

In this diagram, CD = CE.
What is the value of x?
reference_items.figure_description:
A geometric diagram with two triangles, ABC and CDE, meeting at vertex C.
- Segment BD is a horizontal line containing point C between B and D.
- Segment AE is a straight line that intersects line BD at point C.
- Segment AB is vertical and perpendicular to BD, with a right-angle square mark shown at angle ABC.
- Line segment AB extends slightly above point A.
- Angle BAC is marked with an arc and labeled 50°.
- On triangle CDE, segment CD and segment CE each have a single tick mark indicating CD = CE.
- Segment DE connects points D and E.
- Angle CDE at vertex D is marked with an arc.
- Angle DEC at vertex E is marked with an arc and labeled x°.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Regular hexagon PQRSTU]

PQRSTU is a regular hexagon. What is the measure of the angle QUS?
reference_items.figure_description: A regular hexagon with vertices labeled clockwise: P at the top left, Q at the top right, R at the far right, S at the bottom right, T at the bottom left, and U at the far left. Segment PQ forms the top horizontal edge, and segment TS forms the bottom horizontal edge. Two internal straight line segments are drawn: one connecting vertex U to vertex Q, and another connecting vertex U to vertex S, forming angle QUS.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
In this figure, triangles ABC and DEF are congruent with BC = EF .

[Image: Overlapping triangles ABC and DEF]

What is the measure of angle EGC ?
reference_items.figure_description: Two overlapping triangles, ABC and DEF, resting on a shared horizontal baseline containing points B, E, C, and F in that order from left to right. Segment BC is the base of triangle ABC, and segment EF is the base of triangle DEF. Vertex A is above the baseline, and vertex D is to the right of A and also above the baseline. Side AC intersects side DE at point G. Angle B is labeled 40°, and angle F is labeled 60°.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Two triangles]

The triangles shown are congruent. The measures of some of the sides and angles are given. What is the value of x?
reference_items.figure_description:
Two triangles are shown side by side.
The left triangle has a horizontal bottom side. Its left side is labeled "6 cm". The interior angle at the bottom-left vertex is labeled "49°", and the interior angle at the top vertex is labeled "81°".
The right triangle has a nearly horizontal bottom side that slopes slightly downward from right to left, labeled "6 cm". The interior angle at the bottom-right vertex is labeled "81°", and the interior angle at the top vertex is labeled "x°".
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
In the figure, PQ and RS are intersecting straight lines.

[Image: Intersecting lines PQ and RS]

What is the value of x + y ?
reference_items.figure_description: Two straight lines intersect. Line PQ slopes downward from upper-left (point P) to lower-right (point Q). Line RS slopes upward from lower-left (point R) to upper-right (point S). At the intersection, an angle arc indicates the obtuse top angle between ray P and ray S, labeled 150°. An arc indicates the acute angle on the left between ray P and ray R, labeled x°. An arc indicates the acute angle on the right between ray S and ray Q, labeled y°.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: Which shape has a line of symmetry?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: A trapezoid with two parallel horizontal lines. The right side of the trapezoid is longer than the left hand side.]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: An isosceles triangle with the base forming a vertical line.]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: A parallelogram where top and bottom sides are equal in length and the left and right sides are also equal in length.]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: A right triangle with the 90 degree angle in the bottom left.]

reference_items.figure_description:
Four geometric shapes labeled A through D:
A: A trapezoid with horizontal top and bottom parallel sides; the bottom is longer than the top, and the right slanted side is longer and less steep than the left side.
B: An isosceles triangle with a vertical base on the left and a vertex pointing to the right; the top and bottom sides are marked with equal tick marks.
C: A parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides each marked with a single tick mark, and slanted left and right sides each marked with a double tick mark.
D: A scalene right-angled triangle with a vertical left side and a horizontal bottom side, with a right-angle square symbol marked at the lower-left corner.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Two parallel lines, M and N. M lies above N. Two lines are drawn over M and N. One goes up from the left to the right, and the other one goes down, from the left to the right. The two lines intersect N at two different points, but meet at a common point on line M. This forms a triangle between lines M and N. The top angle of this triangle is angle B. The right most angle of this triangle is 70 degrees. The line that goes up from the left to the right intersects line M at a 60 degree angle.]

Lines m and n are parallel.

What is the value of b?

Answer: ____

descriptors: Incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.figure_description: Two horizontal parallel lines with arrows at both ends are labeled m (top line) and n (bottom line). Two intersecting lines cross lines m and n: one line slopes upward from lower left to upper right, and the other slopes downward from upper left to lower right. The two lines intersect each other at a single point on line m, and they cross line n at two separate points, forming a triangle between lines m and n. The top interior angle of this triangle at the intersection point on line m is marked with an arc and labeled b°. The bottom-right interior angle of the triangle along line n is marked with an arc and labeled 70°. Above line m, in the angle between the right side of line m and the upward-sloping line, the angle is marked with an arc and labeled 60°.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration.
